Comparison Summary Claude Fable 5.2 (Max, Default Fallback) is amongst the leading models in intelligence, but particularly expensive when comparing to other models of similar price. It's also notably slow per task and very verbose. The model supports text and image input, outputs text, and has a 1M tokens context window.

Claude Fable 5.2 (Max, Default Fallback) scores 65 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it well above average among comparable models (median: 40). When evaluating the Intelligence Index, it generated 275M tokens, which is very verbose in comparison to the median of 72.8M.

Pricing for Claude Fable 5.2 (Max, Default Fallback) is $8.00 per 1M input tokens (expensive, median: $2.00) and $40.00 per 1M output tokens (expensive, median: $10.00). On average, it costs $26.54 per task to evaluate Claude Fable 5.2 (Max, Default Fallback) on the Intelligence Index.

At 46.4 minutes per Intelligence Index task, Claude Fable 5.2 (Max, Default Fallback) is notably slow compared with the median of 12.7 minutes for comparable models (lower is better).

reactions: [Hacker News] They have it at maxed out reasoning. Go into the dropdown and select high or medium, which are what people actually use. It's a decent bump while both being faster and costing less (per task). The worst thing about AA is defaulting to the highest reasoning value for everything.

[Hacker News] The Semi-analysis analysis piece is quite good: https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/anthropic-subscription... There was some chatter on Twitter, Reddit and here when an earlier version of this came out where people normalized it by completed AA or Epoch task and Claude models still came out well ahead. In practice OpenAI subscriptions are more competitive than they appear bec

[Hacker News] I'm not sure I understand your complaint. The default reasoning effort for Fable on their harness is medium, not max. It also uses the latest version of Fable by default. So a standard user will see a ~10% performance bump, better reasoning, and an ~50% price drop. And they can just... use the old model if they want? How is that bad?

[Hacker News] Very interested if you have any citations for how Claude subscriptions give "much better value". I've recently been researching this with mixed analysis. It seems like most analysis is basically "how many tokens do you get with a subscription and how much would those tokens cost at API rates".
